tagline: 17,000 islands across three time zones — the world's largest archipelagic state.
summary: Indonesia is the largest archipelago on Earth: more than 17,000 islands stretching 3,200 nautical miles from Sumatra to Papua, home to 280 million people. Movement between its islands is the spine of national life and the engine of its tourism economy. Today that movement runs on slow RoRo ferries, weather-exposed fast boats, and short-hop domestic flights. A clean, stabilised foiling tier is the premium-but-practical layer the archipelago has never had.
why_marine_mobility: No single city brief captures Indonesia, because the nation IS the water between Bali, Lombok, the Gilis, Flores and Komodo. The Bali–Lombok crossing alone carries enormous tourist and resort traffic on fast boats that cancel in heavy swell; the run east to Komodo and the dragons is a multi-day expedition no day-boat can shorten. Navier's Pioneer II foiling tier turns a pounding 90-minute fast-boat ride into a smooth, dry glide, and the Quanta-LR hybrid range opens the long eastern trunk toward Flores and Komodo that battery craft cannot reach.

use_cases.body: Bali to Lombok and the Gilis: replace the rough, frequently-cancelled fast-boat transfer with a smooth, dry, weather-resilient foiling crossing between two of the country's busiest tourist islands.
Serangan to Teluk Nare: a discreet premium link for the Bali and north-Lombok ultra-luxury resort belt, sized comfortably inside Pioneer II range.
Lombok to Komodo: a long-range Quanta-LR trunk toward Labuan Bajo and the Komodo National Park — the eastern expedition corridor that no battery day-boat can serve.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The core resort corridors — Bali–Lombok (55 nm), Lombok–Gili chain, and the Labuan Bajo–Komodo island hops (~20–25 nm) — sit inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots, commercial-ready today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The long eastern trunk — Lombok toward Komodo / Flores (200+ nm) — is Quanta-LR territory (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+), opening expedition corridors no day-boat can reach.

signature_routes.label: Bali ↔ Lombok — the headline resort crossing
Lombok ↔ Komodo — the eastern long-range expedition trunk
Komodo ↔ Gili Lawa — the national-park island hop

transit_planning: For a luxury-resort operator or a super-app: a premium, low-emission water tier that makes the most-travelled resort crossings dry, smooth and weather-resilient, and gives ultra-luxury properties a discreet transfer their guests will pay for. Start with the proven Bali–Lombok–Gili corridors on Pioneer II, then extend the eastern Flores/Komodo trunk on Quanta-LR as range comes online.
competitive_landscape: Inter-island travel today splits between domestic aviation (fast but skips the journey and clogs regional airports), conventional RoRo ferries (affordable but slow), and tourist fast boats (quicker but rough, wet and cancellation-prone in swell). Navier's foiling tier is the missing premium-but-practical middle: faster than any ferry, smoother and drier than any fast boat, cleaner than both.
regulatory_note: Domestic sea transport is regulated by the Directorate General of Sea Transportation under the Ministry of Transportation (Kementerian Perhubungan); commercial inter-island operation requires vessel registration and route licensing. Bali and Nusa Tenggara Barat (Lombok) provincial transport authorities are natural first regional touchpoints.
seasonality: The dry season (Apr–Oct) brings the calmest seas across Bali, Lombok and the Lesser Sundas; the wet season (Nov–Mar) raises swell and fast-boat cancellations — precisely where a stabilised foiling craft holds its schedule.

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium water-shuttle model Navier brings to Indonesia's resort islands.
